newsitem.title: UK: Southnews shares up on upbeat prospects.
newsitem.headline: Southnews shares up on upbeat prospects.

text.p: Shares in Southnews Plc set a record high on Wednesday after the company posted a 36 percent rise in first-half year pre-tax profit and said it expected the improvement to continue through the rest of the year.
The shares were quoted up 15-1/2p at 463p by 1244 GMT -- surpassing the previous record of 447-1/2p set yesterday -- though no trading was recorded in the stock.
"The board believes that our plans for organic growth and linked acquisition benefits are proceeding well," said chairman Gareth Clark.
"Consequently, assuming a stable economic environment, we anticipate that the significant improvements made in the year to date will continue throghout the financial year."
The company said the results were boosted by the first time inclusion of recently acquired Croydon Advertiser Group.
Pretax profit increased to 2.68 million stg from 1.97 million stg in the same period last year and Southnews posted a 28 percent rise in its interim dividend to 2.25p per share.
The company said revenues rose 39 percent to 18.4 million stg from 13.2 million stg in the first six months of last year.

It said borrowings had been reduced by strong positive cash flow and the group had secured and improved market share by implementing new ideas, systems and equipment as well as benefitting from stronger economic activity.
It added that recruitment and other classified advertising had been strong.
